instructions:
1. Kneel and place your forearms on the floor, clasping your hands to form a triangle.
2. Set the crown of your head on the floor against your clasped hands.
3. Walk your feet in until your hips stack over your shoulders.
4. Engage your core and slowly lift both legs until your body is vertical.
5. Hold the position, pressing your forearms down to keep weight off your neck.
6. Lower your legs with control to exit. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press firmly through your forearms so most of your weight rests on your arms, not your head.
2. Keep your core braced to prevent the lower back from arching.
3. Never kick up with momentum; lift slowly to protect your neck.
4. Practice against a wall until your balance is reliable.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball.
2. Press the ball straight overhead with both arms extended.
3. Brace your core and keep your ribs down to avoid arching your back.
4. Hold the ball steady directly above your shoulders.
5. Lower the ball with control once the hold time is complete. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the ball stacked over your shoulders, not in front of your head.
2. Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs to keep the torso stable.
3. Breathe steadily throughout the hold.
4. Choose a weight you can hold with full arm extension.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
2. Brace your core and keep your elbows tucked.
3. Press the ball straight out in front of your chest until your arms are extended.
4. Pause briefly with the ball at arm's length.
5. Pull the ball back to your chest with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the press path level and aimed at chest height.
2. Brace your abs so your torso does not lean back.
3. Move with control on the return rather than letting the ball drop in.
4. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands clasped in front of your chest.
2. Lower into a squat until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
3. Jump up and land softly in a wider squat stance, thighs parallel.
4. Jump again and land back in the narrow hip-width squat.
5. Continue alternating between wide and narrow squats. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly on the balls of your feet to absorb impact.
2. Keep your knees tracking over your toes on every landing.
3. Brace your core and keep your chest lifted throughout.
4. Move quickly but stay in control of each landing.
